$comment: Sector norm for row 74 (quality_process_maturity): which management-system certification peers are expected to hold, by ATECO prefix (digits only, dots ignored; the longest matching prefix wins; the generic baseline applies when nothing more specific matches). 'Gap vs sector norm' = none of expected_any_of held. The standards named are the brief's own examples; the ATECO prefixes they are attached to are the ASSISTANT'S MAPPING (status TO_CALIBRATE) and must be confirmed by GG. No peer prevalence figure was invented: every threshold below is TO_CALIBRATE.

thresholds.note: Prevalence figures need real peer data (e.g. Accredia certified-organisation counts by ATECO); the other two define 'long held, multi-standard' for the READINESS mapping. Until set, a certified firm that meets the norm is labelled certified_meets_norm, never long_held_multi_standard.

generic_baseline.basis: Brief: ISO 9001 as the generic baseline.

sector_norms.basis: Brief example: IATF 16949 for automotive suppliers. ATECO division 29 (motor vehicles, trailers, parts) is the assistant's mapping.
Brief example: AS9100 for aerospace. ATECO 30.3 (aircraft and spacecraft) is the assistant's mapping; EN 9100 listed as the European equivalent (assumption).

Brief example: ISO 3834 or EN 15085 for welding and rail. ATECO 30.2 (rail rolling stock) and 25.1 (structural metal products) are the assistant's mapping; other welded-fabrication codes are not covered.
